veranderings.blok: Vier dinge vir 'n plant wat groei
veranderings.voor: Hierdie vier dinge het enige groen plant nodig wat al bo die grond groei.
veranderings.na: Enige groen plant wat al bo die grond groei, het hierdie vier dinge nodig.
veranderings.rede: With the object fronted and the relative clause split from its noun, a Grade 4 reader can mistake which is the subject; subject-first order is clearer.

veranderings.voor: bleek en die stam lank en swak
veranderings.na: bleek, en die stam word lank en swak
veranderings.rede: Three 'en's in a row blur where the second clause starts; repeating the verb makes it a full clause, which then takes the AWS comma.

veranderings.voor: Water is een van hierdie vier dinge
veranderings.na: Water is een van die vier dinge
veranderings.rede: 'hierdie' points back to a list that is not in this block; 'die vier dinge' refers to it naturally.

veranderings.voor: Die wortels suig water uit die grond na die res van die plant.
veranderings.na: Die wortels suig water uit die grond op, en die water gaan na die res van die plant.
veranderings.rede: 'suig ... na die res van die plant' is unidiomatic, since sucking draws towards the one sucking; splitting it keeps both steps of the meaning.

veranderings.blok: Lug by die blare en die wortels
veranderings.voor: Die blare kry lug bo die grond en die wortels
veranderings.na: Die blare kry lug bo die grond, en die wortels
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: a comma goes before 'en' that joins two sentences, each with its own subject and verb.

veranderings.blok: Lug by die blare en die wortels
veranderings.voor: Grond wat heeltyd papnat bly laat
veranderings.na: Grond wat heeltyd papnat bly, laat
veranderings.rede: A comma between the relative clause's verb and the main verb ('bly, laat') stops the two verbs running together, as in 'In grond wat papnat bly, kom' later in the lesson.

veranderings.voor: met 'n paar blare aan heet 'n steggie
veranderings.na: met 'n paar blare daaraan word 'n steggie genoem
veranderings.rede: A bare 'aan' at the end of the phrase is colloquial and 'heet' is stiff for Grade 4; 'daaraan' and 'word ... genoem' are the natural forms.

veranderings.voor: maak baie maklik wortels op hierdie manier
veranderings.na: maak op hierdie manier baie maklik wortels
veranderings.rede: In Afrikaans the adverbial of manner sits more naturally before the object than trailing at the end.
'voor hom gegroei' (grew before it, the seed) reads awkwardly and 'hom' for the seed clashes with 'dit' elsewhere; 'al voorheen' keeps the meaning.
'binne-in' is the natural form for 'inside' at the end of a clause, and the lesson uses it elsewhere.

veranderings.voor: moet sy eerste worteltjie en blare nog uitstoot
veranderings.na: moet nog sy eerste worteltjie en blare uitstoot
veranderings.rede: 'nog' belongs right after the modal verb; putting it after the object is unnatural.

veranderings.voor: Ontkieming is die woord vir 'n saad wat oopbars en begin groei.
veranderings.na: Ontkieming is wanneer 'n saad oopbars en begin groei.
veranderings.rede: As written, the word names the seed rather than the process; the change matches the glossary's 'Wanneer 'n saad oopbars'.

veranderings.voor: Eers suig die saad water in en dan swel dit dikker op.
veranderings.na: Eers suig die saad water in, en dan swel dit op.
veranderings.rede: AWS comma between two full clauses joined by 'en'; 'swel op' already means 'gets thicker', so 'dikker' is redundant and wooden.
'ondertoe' is the standard one-word form and matches 'boontoe' in the next sentence.

veranderings.blok: Wat 'n saad nodig het om te ontkiem
veranderings.rede: The same block refers to the seed as 'dit' ('voordat dit kan ontkiem'); keep the pronoun consistent.

veranderings.voor: 'n Saad en 'n plant wat groei het nie
veranderings.na: 'n Saad en 'n plant wat groei, het nie
veranderings.rede: Without the comma, 'groei het' runs the relative clause's verb into the main verb and the sentence is hard to parse.

veranderings.voor: Water, lug en warmte het die saad en die plant wat groei albei nodig.
veranderings.na: Die saad en die plant wat groei, het albei water, lug en warmte nodig.
veranderings.rede: With the object fronted, it is unclear who needs what; subject first is clearer and keeps every word of the meaning.

veranderings.blok: Wat om te meet en aan te teken
veranderings.voor: Tel hoeveel blare die plantjie elke week het.
veranderings.na: Tel elke week hoeveel blare die plantjie het.
veranderings.rede: 'elke week' belongs with the instruction 'tel' (count weekly), not inside the counted clause.

veranderings.voor: Hoe sal jy kan sien watter een
veranderings.na: Hoe kan jy sien watter een
veranderings.rede: The double modal 'sal ... kan' is heavy for Grade 4; 'Hoe kan jy sien' says the same thing.

vlae.teks: So 'n plant verlep heeltemal en gaan later dood.
vlae.rede: The condition (the soil stays dry even longer) is only implied, so the sentence can read as saying every drooping plant dies; restoring it means choosing content, so it goes to the writer.

vlae.teks: Jy plant twee sade. Die een pot staan in die warm son en die ander een in 'n koue kamer.
vlae.rede: 'Die een pot' has no antecedent, because pots were never mentioned; fixing it means adding that each seed is in its own pot, which is a content choice.

vlae.teks: Kyk elke week mooi wat met die twee plantjies gebeur.
vlae.rede: The block plants 'n paar boontjies' plus one cutting, so 'die twee plantjies' does not match what was planted; probably the two pots are meant, but correcting it means guessing the intent.
